To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the N170 component of the ERP to faces has the same topography for human and animal faces, but a later latency for the latter, and a different topography for faces and objects in the N170 time-window.

the N170 is not specific for human faces, but rather reflects the processing of facial stimuli, and that the N170 topography is different for faces compared with objects, but similar for human and animal faces.
the N170 is sensitive to the facial organization of animal faces, that it is not a specific index of human faces and that its scalp distribution is not specific to faces.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the N170 in the context of a more complex scene.
the neural basis of the processing of human and animal faces in the context of other objects.
the study of the human brain activity when processing visual information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
N170 is a face-selective component that is also sensitive to the presence of a face-like configuration.
the human face processing is not specific to the N170 component, but that this component is a good indicator of face processing.
N170 is not a face-specific response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the N170 is not specific to human faces and is probably not a unitary component but a set of overlapping components with a similar scalp distribution.
the N170 is sensitive to the presence of faces and to the face category, but it is not sensitive to the presence or the category of other objects.
the N170 is a face-specific component in the context in which faces appear in natural scenes, but it is also sensitive to animal faces and to objects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the N170 is not a pure human faces-specific component but that the face activity in the N170 time-window has a different topography for human and animal faces compared with objects.
the N170 is not specific to human faces, but is a more general response to facial features.
it is important to use the same stimuli and experimental design when comparing ERP components across studies.
